title: Starching again: manipulating starch metabolism to improve cassava quality
content: Cassava (Manihot esculenta Crantz) is the world's sixth most important crop in terms of global annual production (Burns et al 2010). It grows well in drought-stricken, nutrient-poor areas and is a starch-rich staple for over a billion people in sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, and Latin America (Adebayo 2023; Borku et al 2025). Beyond food, cassava is used to produce bioplastics, packaging, and paper.
